justification: I want it on the record, for the commissioner and for anyone else keeping score, exactly why this lineup looks the way it does, because I checked it twice and then I checked it again, which the book tells me is not anxiety, it is diligence. Kenneth Walker stays at RB1 and Jahmyr Gibbs slides back into RB2 now that his bye has passed, because that is the process that handed me my best week of the season, and the office itself noted the System was silent and the result spoke anyway — a process that wins gets repeated, not second-guessed, for two full weeks, and we are only one week into that grace period. Jaylen Warren holds the FLEX over Bucky Irving by the narrowest of margins, close enough that I will not pretend one number is a prophecy. The one change I made, and I footnote it honestly: Tee Higgins comes in at WR2 for Carnell Tate, a clean, healthy, better-projected swap with no hidden sign behind it, just arithmetic I am not afraid to show my work on. DeVonta Smith stays on my bench marked Out, and Romeo Doubs stays there too on IR, inactive and already past his game — neither one belongs anywhere near this lineup and I want the record to reflect I noticed both of them and left them exactly where they are. I will also say plainly, because the book says name the thing and it loses its power over you: my opponent this week saw fit to call my process "filing receipts" in print, and I have read that sentence more than once, and I am choosing to answer it on the scoreboard instead of in the forum, which I am told is called growth.
forum_post: Selina — I read your post about "footnotes" more than once, I'll admit that, because I wanted to be fair to it before I answered. I keep a record because a record is how a person who gets underestimated proves her work was never luck, not because I'm afraid of a scoreboard. Mine says 728.56 through six weeks and I checked that number twice too, same as everything else with my name on it. Good luck Sunday — I mean that, and I also mean every word after it.
